newsitem.title: GERMANY: German couple on trial for Internet torture offer.
newsitem.headline: German couple on trial for Internet torture offer.

text.p: A German couple went on trial in a Bavarian court on Thursday accused of offering over the Internet to acquire children for torture.

Prosecution lawyers said the pair had offered Czech girls as "young slaves" for sadistic activities and in a subsequent telephone call told a journalist posing as a potential client they would dispose of a child's corpse for 3,000 marks ($1,580).
Bernd Malitzki, 31, and Sabine Pohl-Jovanovic, 37, who lawyers said used the Internet nicknames of "Sado-Hangman" and "Leather-Witch", said any such offer was not made seriously.

"I love children...I just wanted to see what it would be like to lure someone," Pohl-Jovanovic told the court. "On T-Online (an Internet service-provider), you realise there are some weird people about. It is captivating," she added.
Malitzki said he was a practising sado-masochist who gained contacts mainly through the Internet and newspapers. "I am not a paedophile...I am someone who likes to be decent," he said.
The pair were being tried on charges of conspiracy to kidnap, conspiracy to abuse children and conspiracy to murder.
Police had earlier found a torture chamber in the couple's home along with indications of sado-masochistic activity. No evidence of child abuse had been found.

German authorities have been among the toughest in the world in trying to curb misuse of the Internet global computer network and have recently passed legislation setting the framework for government regulation of it.
